Corn___Common_Rust.description: La roya común es una enfermedad fúngica causada por Puccinia sorghi, que provoca pústulas de color marrón canela en la superficie de las hojas.
symptoms: Pústulas de color marrón canela en la superficie superior e inferior de las hojas.
Las hojas se vuelven amarillas y pueden marchitarse prematuramente.
Las pústulas se vuelven de color marrón oscuro a negro a medida que el cultivo madura.
treatment: Aplique fungicidas a base de cobre o triazol recomendados al principio de la temporada.
Evite el riego por aspersión aérea para mantener el dosel seco.
Asegure un espaciado adecuado de los cultivos para mejorar la ventilación.
prevention: Utilice semillas de maíz híbrido resistentes a la roya.
Practique una rotación de cultivos adecuada con cultivos no hospedantes.
Mantenga una salud óptima del suelo con una aplicación equilibrada de nitrógeno.

Corn___Gray_Leaf_Spot.description: [ES] Gray leaf spot is a fungal disease caused by Cercospora zeae-maydis. It causes rectangular lesions along the veins of corn leaves.
symptoms: [ES] Rectangular, gray-to-tan lesions restricted by leaf veins.
[ES] Lesions coalesce to kill entire leaf blades under hot and humid conditions.
[ES] Severe leaf blighting leading to stalk lodging and yield loss.
treatment: [ES] Apply strobilurin or triazole fungicides at the first sign of lesions.
[ES] Mow or till fields to accelerate the decomposition of residue.
[ES] Ensure balanced soil potash nutrition.
prevention: [ES] Select resistant hybrids with strong Gray Leaf Spot scores.
[ES] Practice a two-year crop rotation with soy or wheat.
[ES] Avoid no-till farming in fields with a history of the disease.

Corn___Healthy.description: [ES] The corn foliage is healthy, showing bright green leaves with no symptoms of fungal or bacterial infections.
symptoms: [ES] Leaves are vibrant green without any lesions or spots.
[ES] Firm stalks and normal grain development.
[ES] Uniform crop growth and dense canopy.
treatment: [ES] No active treatment required.
[ES] Continue standard irrigation and fertilizing routines.
prevention: [ES] Maintain periodic field scouting.
[ES] Follow balanced fertilizer application guidelines.
[ES] Avoid stress conditions like over or under-watering.

Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: [ES] Northern corn leaf blight (NCLB) is a destructive fungal disease caused by Exserohilum turcicum, producing large cigar-shaped lesions.
symptoms: [ES] Long, elliptical, cigar-shaped grayish-green or tan lesions.
[ES] Lesions appear first on lower leaves and move upwards.
[ES] Dirty green to dark gray dust-like spores on lesions during wet weather.
treatment: [ES] Spray triazole or strobilurin-based fungicides during silking.
[ES] Ensure thorough deep plowing of infected residue after harvest.
[ES] Incorporate crop rotation with soybean.
prevention: [ES] Plant NCLB-resistant corn hybrids.
[ES] Clean tillage tools before entering new fields.
[ES] Maintain optimal balanced plant nutrition.

Potato___Early_Blight.description: [ES] Early blight is caused by the fungus Alternaria solani. It affects leaves, stems, and tubers, producing dark target-like spots.
symptoms: [ES] Dark brown spots with concentric rings (target board pattern) on older leaves.
[ES] Spots enlarge and cause leaf yellowing and dropping.
[ES] Leathery, sunken black spots on potato tubers.
treatment: [ES] Apply protectant fungicides like Mancozeb or Chlorothalonil.
[ES] Remove volunteer potato plants and nightshade weeds.
[ES] Apply organic mulch to reduce soil splash.
prevention: [ES] Use high-quality, certified disease-free seed tubers.
[ES] Ensure proper crop spacing and avoid overhead watering.
[ES] Rotate with non-solanaceous crops (e.g., corn, grass).

Potato___Healthy.description: [ES] The potato crop is healthy, showing vigorous green leaves and sturdy stems with no signs of blights or rot.
symptoms: [ES] Lush green, fully expanded leaves with no necrotic spots.
[ES] Sturdy upright stalks and healthy root systems.
[ES] Normal tuber skin coloration.
treatment: [ES] No treatment required.
[ES] Ensure proper hilling (mounding soil around plants) and uniform watering.
prevention: [ES] Scout fields weekly for symptoms.
[ES] Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization late in the season.
[ES] Use clean irrigation water.

Potato___Late_Blight.description: [ES] Late blight is caused by the oomycete Phytophthora infestans. It is highly destructive and thrives in cool, wet weather.
symptoms: [ES] Dark, water-soaked lesions on leaves that expand rapidly.
[ES] White, fuzzy fungal growth on the underside of leaves in wet conditions.
[ES] Tubers develop brown-to-purple dry rot and decay quickly.
treatment: [ES] Spray systemic fungicides containing Metalaxyl or Dimethomorph immediately.
[ES] Destroy all infected crops and piles of discarded potatoes.
[ES] Harvest only in dry weather and store carefully.
prevention: [ES] Plant late blight-resistant potato cultivars.
[ES] Use certified disease-free seed potato tubers.
[ES] Ensure good soil cover (hilling) to protect developing tubers from spores.

Rice___Brown_Spot.description: [ES] Brown spot is a fungal disease caused by Bipolaris oryzae. It often targets crops growing in nutrient-deficient or poorly drained soils.
symptoms: [ES] Small, oval-to-circular brown lesions with yellow halos on leaves.
[ES] Large lesions dry up and cover the entire leaf blade.
[ES] Brown discoloration on rice grains leading to poor seed quality.
treatment: [ES] Apply trace element fertilizers (specifically zinc and potassium).
[ES] Spray fungicides like Propiconazole or Hexaconazole if severity increases.
[ES] Practice proper soil drainage to avoid waterlogging.
prevention: [ES] Use certified disease-resistant rice varieties.
[ES] Apply balanced NPK fertilization alongside micronutrients.
[ES] Keep fields weed-free to prevent spore transfer.

Rice___Healthy.description: [ES] The rice crop shows excellent vegetative growth, with erect green leaves and uniform plant height, indicating no symptoms of blast or leaf spots.
symptoms: [ES] Erect, uniform green leaf blades with no visible lesions.
[ES] Healthy root system in flooded or moist soils.
[ES] Normal panicle development during heading.
treatment: [ES] No treatment required.
[ES] Maintain consistent shallow flooding depth (2-5 cm) as per crop stage.
prevention: [ES] Monitor water quality and maintain proper NPK ratios.
[ES] Remove alternative grass hosts from field bunds.
[ES] Implement line planting for uniform light and aeration.

Rice___Leaf_Blast.description: [ES] Leaf blast is a highly critical fungal disease caused by Magnaporthe oryzae. It can lead to severe crop failure in susceptible varieties under humid conditions.
symptoms: [ES] Diamond-shaped (spindle) lesions on leaves with gray centers and brown borders.
[ES] Lesions enlarge and coalesce, burning or drying the leaves.
[ES] Lesions can also appear on the collar of leaves.
treatment: [ES] Apply systemic fungicides like Tricyclazole or Kasugamycin immediately.
[ES] Reduce nitrogen fertilizer application to limit disease spread.
[ES] Maintain continuous standing water in the field to buffer temperature.
prevention: [ES] Sow blast-resistant varieties like IR36 or local resistant hybrids.
[ES] Avoid late sowing to bypass optimal weather for fungal growth.
[ES] Use silicon-based amendments to strengthen plant resistance.

Rice___Neck_Blast.description: [ES] Neck blast occurs when Magnaporthe oryzae infects the neck node of the panicle, leading to broken necks and empty grain hulls.
symptoms: [ES] Grayish-brown lesions on the neck node of the panicle.
[ES] Neck rots and breaks, causing the panicle to fall over.
[ES] Grains fail to fill, appearing white, empty, and light.
treatment: [ES] Spray systemic fungicides like Tricyclazole or Isoprothiolane at late booting/early heading stage.
[ES] Harvest early if neck blast is widespread to save remaining grains.
[ES] Ensure fields are not dried out during flowering.
prevention: [ES] Avoid excessive nitrogen application at booting stage.
[ES] Use high-quality silicon amendments.
[ES] Practice thorough residue removal and field sterilization.

Sugarcane___Bacterial_Blight.description: [ES] Bacterial leaf blight of sugarcane is caused by Xanthomonas albilineans. It targets the vascular system of the cane, leading to leaf scalding and stalk death.
symptoms: [ES] Cream-to-yellow stripes on leaves parallel to veins.
[ES] Stripes turn reddish-brown and leaves wither from the tip.
[ES] Internal stalk tissue shows red vascular bundles when cut.
treatment: [ES] Use hot water treatment (50°C for 2 hours) on seed canes before planting.
[ES] Spray copper hydroxide bactericide to reduce surface bacteria.
[ES] Isolate and burn infected crop clumps immediately.
prevention: [ES] Plant disease-resistant sugarcane varieties.
[ES] Sanitize knives and harvesting tools with disinfectants between plants.
[ES] Improve field drainage to prevent bacterial transport in water.

Sugarcane___Healthy.description: [ES] The sugarcane stalks are robust and filled, foliage is dark green, with no signs of smut, red rot, or wilt.
symptoms: [ES] Wide, green, healthy leaves with clean midribs.
[ES] Thick, filled, and hard stalks with normal internode length.
[ES] Healthy root system and normal tillering.
treatment: [ES] No active treatment required.
[ES] Apply timely nitrogen and potassium fertilizers based on growth phase.
prevention: [ES] Practice regular earthing up to support cane weight.
[ES] Remove dry leaves (detrash) at 5th and 7th months to allow aeration.
[ES] Monitor for early pests like borers.

Sugarcane___Red_Rot.description: [ES] Red rot is caused by the fungus Colletotrichum falcatum. It is known as the 'cancer of sugarcane' and causes severe internal rot.
symptoms: [ES] Third or fourth leaf shows yellowing and dry margins.
[ES] Splitting the cane reveals internal red pith with white cross bands.
[ES] Characteristic alcoholic smell from affected split canes.
treatment: [ES] Uproot the entire infected clump, spray the spot with lime, and burn the residue.
[ES] Apply Trichoderma bio-fungicide to the soil.
[ES] Harvest the field immediately if infection is widespread.
prevention: [ES] Grow resistant varieties (like Co 86032 or local equivalents).
[ES] Practice crop rotation with rice or green manure crops.
[ES] Use healthy seed canes treated with bio-agents.

Wheat___Brown_Rust.description: [ES] Brown rust (leaf rust) is caused by Puccinia triticina. It is the most common wheat rust, forming small orange-brown pustules on leaf blades.
symptoms: [ES] Small, round, orange-brown pustules scattered randomly on leaves.
[ES] Pustules rub off as a brown powder (spores) on fingers.
[ES] Rapid defoliation under warm (15-25°C) and humid weather.
treatment: [ES] Spray propiconazole or tebuconazole fungicides at the first appearance of rust.
[ES] Ensure balanced potash nutrition to improve plant immunity.
[ES] Avoid high seeding density to reduce humidity inside canopy.
prevention: [ES] Cultivate resistant wheat varieties.
[ES] Sow early to avoid warm temperatures during grain filling.
[ES] Control volunteer wheat crops that carry the spores over summer.

Wheat___Healthy.description: [ES] The wheat crop is in excellent condition, leaves are uniform green with no powdery mildew or rust pustules.
symptoms: [ES] Uniform green leaf blades without yellowing or spots.
[ES] Strong erect stems and healthy green spikes.
[ES] No signs of wilting or head abnormalities.
treatment: [ES] No treatment required.
[ES] Ensure timely irrigation during critical stages like crown root initiation and flowering.
prevention: [ES] Maintain weed-free boundaries.
[ES] Apply nitrogen fertilizer in splits to prevent nitrogen stress.
[ES] Ensure proper crop rotation.

Wheat___Yellow_Rust.description: [ES] Yellow rust (stripe rust) is caused by Puccinia striiformis. It forms yellow stripes of pustules on leaves, thriving in cooler conditions.
symptoms: [ES] Yellow-to-orange pustules arranged in narrow, long stripes along leaf veins.
[ES] Affected leaf blades dry up and turn brown rapidly.
[ES] Stunted plant growth and shriveled grains.
treatment: [ES] Apply systemic fungicides such as Propiconazole or Triadimefon immediately.
[ES] Increase potassium fertilizer to support recovery.
[ES] Scout and isolate early infected patches.
prevention: [ES] Plant yellow rust-resistant wheat varieties.
[ES] Avoid late sowing to minimize exposure to cool humid conditions.
[ES] Ensure proper crop rotation.
